newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian soccer team the Socceroos will face the world-champions Brazil in the Confederations Cup in Saudi Arabia in December. The draw on Saturday night was not a good one for Australia, as they will have to also play Asian champions Saudi Arabia and North American champions, Mexico.

Australian Football League team Geelong moved into the second round of the Ansett Cup for the first time since 1992 after beating the West Coast Eagles at Waverley on Saturday night. Despite the win, coach Gary Eyres cited performance, effort and honesty as the major factors he was looking for in the Cat's game.

Young Western Australian batsman Ryan Campbell set the WACA ground ablaze yesterday smashing the season's fastest half century off only 32 balls. The opener took only 38 minutes to reach his fifty, hitting 10 boundaries and one six in his majestic inning.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Olympic gold medallist Linford Christie had to struggle to win the Botany Bay Gift in Sydney yesterday. The 36-year-old champion won A$24,000 in prize money with his A$10,000 appearance fee, and said next year, if he competes, he wants a head start, which he said should be determined by age.

Australian Rugby League officials will make a decision whether video replays will be used in all games this season after an embarrassing glitch in Saturday night's match between Manly and Newcastle. Referee Kelvin Jeffes awarded a "no try" to Craig Innes and called for a scrum, only for the scoreboard to flash "fair try" whilst it was packing.

Melbourne Cup winning jockey Damien Oliver is almost assured of a race on classy colt Schubert in next month's Golden Slipper after connections of the horse sacked Rod Griffiths following a rough race by the jockey in the Blue Diamond Stakes on Saturday. Trainer Peter Hayes said Griffith's "slaughtered" Schubert after he sat four or five-wide during the race.
THE AGE

The Australian cricket team looks certain to go into the first test against South Africa with two pace bowlers and two spinners after an impressive victory against Natal in Durban. All rounder Michael Bevan continued his good form with the ball taking seven wickets for the match. Page 2.

Richmond will meet the winner of tonight's match between North Melbourne and the Western Bulldogs in the second round of the Ansett Cup, after disposing of Hawthorn 11.12.(78) to 9.12.(66) at Waverley Park last night. A third term blitz from the Tigers saw them draw more than three goals clear by the final change. Page 3.

The Western Australia Warriors will go into the final of the Mercantile Cup cricket after a close victory against Victoria in Perth yesterday. Victoria made a strong comeback to finish for 191 but the Warriors cruised to the target in only 42.5 overs after a middle order collapse. Page 7.
THE HERALD SUN

Hockey gold medallist Nova Peris-Kneebone made a successful transition to sprinting yesterday, taking out the Botany Bay Gift in Sydney. Starting off 4.75 metres, Peris-Kneebone ran the 120 metres in 12.90 seconds defeating race favourite Melinda Gainsfod who ran fourth. Page 86.

Australian doubles champion Todd Woodbridge advanced to the final of the St Jude classic in Memphis yesterday with a 6-1, 7-5 victory against Swede Jonas Borgman. The win followed Woodbridge's victory with partner Mark Woodforde in the doubles quarter fial. Woodbridge will meet Michael Chang in the singles final today. Page 86.

The Essendon Bombers are confident ruck-rover Chris Daniher will play in their Ansett Cup match against Brisbane at the Gabba next Monday. Daniher suffered a severely bruised arm into the third quarter of Saturday's practice match against Sydney at North Hobart Oval. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Peter Senior won a dramatic play off against New Zealander Steve Alker to win the Canon Challenge at Terry Hills yesterday. After shooting a final round 70, Senior made a birdie on the fourth play-off hole in front of a huge gallery, following three pars for the two men on the play-off 18th. Page 31.

Newcastle Knights player Marc Glanville will face the Australian Rugby League tribunal after an alleged spear tackle on Manly forward Mark Carroll in Coffs Harbour on Saturday night. Carroll has been nursing a badly swollen eye since the incident. The game ended in a 14-all draw. Page 35.

The Melbourne Redbacks has started the season in winning fashion in the 1997 hockey league with two wins over the struggling New South Wales side. The Redbacks defeated the Warriors 3-2 and 4-1 in the opening round of the Fox Sports Cup to take an early ead in the premiership. Page 35.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
